findings.title: A new issuer can bind an inactive or replaced waiver grant and obtain a lease
findings.diagnosis: issuerWaiversChanged maps every pre-issuer GRANT digest to its scope without replaying intervening withdrawal, expiration, or regrant. It then checks only operations after the issuer. Real Apply accepts the stale bound digest, the store reloads the chain, and DeriveLease returns ReasonNone. A valid current-generation control also returns ReasonNone. This violates the active-waiver binding and fail-closed provenance requirements. It does not demonstrate revival of the old issuer without a fresh human approval. A separate control accepts duplicate bound references; duplication alone has not been shown to widen permission.

evidence.observation: The prefix scan records every historic GRANT. The invalidation scan starts at issuer+1.

withdrawn and expired: Apply sequence 7, projected waiver_scope_active=false, lease_active=true. old_after_regrant: Apply sequence 8, scope active under a different grant, old bound grant still active as a lease. current_after_regrant passes as a positive control.
The same three negative controls fail under -race. The current-generation positive control passes.
Preserved real store-loaded chain, presented plan and contract, bound grant, and observed active flags.
Preserved legal grant/withdraw/regrant chain with a fresh issuing approval bound to the replaced grant.

fix.action: Replay waiver history up to each issuer into a live grant-digest map keyed by canonical scope. Require every bound digest to identify the live grant generation at that issuer. Reject missing, expired, withdrawn, replaced, duplicate, or ambiguous references. Preserve the existing after-issuer invalidation scan. Share the check with transition admission where practical.
fix.why: The current helper records all historic GRANT digests, then scans only records after issuance. It never checks whether the referenced grant was still live at issuance. Approval admission does not close this gap.

verification.method: Run TestAuditRealApplyWaiverGeneration in normal and race modes.
verification.expected: withdrawn, expired, and old_after_regrant refuse at Apply or DeriveLease; current_after_regrant remains active.

verification.method: Run TestAuditWaiverAfterIssuer and TestAuditWaiverInvalidAtIssuer in normal and race modes.
verification.expected: Bound withdrawal/expiry/replacement never revive old issuers. Unbound and unrelated controls remain active. Current valid issuers pass. Missing, malformed, and duplicate references refuse.

verification.method: Run full go test ./..., go vet ./..., go test -race ./... with matched TMPDIR and GOTMPDIR.
verification.expected: All regressions pass; legacy approval bytes remain identical.

fix.tradeoffs: Preserving grant identity needs more than the existing boolean active-scope projection. Legacy snapshots without an unambiguous grant digest must fail closed for bound provenance. Existing invalid chains may stop obtaining leases after the fix. No approval field or digest format needs to change.
fix.alternative: For temporary containment, refuse all waiver-bound leases until grant-generation replay exists. This is conservative and blocks valid waived work. An admission-only fix is insufficient for historic accepted issuers unless those chains are explicitly invalidated.

limitations: This is a local code and outcome audit under the trusted-host model. It is not a proof of all possible histories.

This session starts from the user audit brief and neutral closure criteria. Prior audit directories, implementer handoff, and prior verdicts were not read before Phase 1 was frozen. Natural source comments and test names mention earlier finding IDs; they were treated as audited data.

The model/provider/access route is declared by the dispatch brief (liz / gpt-6.1-sol / high / review mode); independent host attestation is not available in this session. No nested agents, CLIs, or model APIs were invoked.
No approved Jev tool is exposed. Auditor judgment is the documented fallback; it grants no authority.
D3-D6 reservations, launches, criterion credit, findings disposition, and architecture amendment are excluded. The audit does not authorize execution, a stage transition, a commit, or release.
Tests ran in a byte-verified repository copy without .git. Test-created temporary Git fixtures are confined to the audit area in final runs. The target repository was read-only throughout.

Early full-suite attempts used unsuitable temporary-directory settings. One race invocation also picked up temporary auditor test files before those were moved to an overlay. Those attempts are retained as diagnostic evidence and superseded by clean final baseline runs.
